name: AIM (AOL Instant Messenger)
blurb: AOL's chat app of screen names, buddy lists and away messages, 1997–2017
title: AIM (AOL Instant Messenger): Away Messages and Why It Shut Down
description: AIM, AOL Instant Messenger, was the chat app of buddy lists, screen names and away messages. It launched in May 1997 and AOL shut it down on December 15, 2017.
answer: AIM was AOL's free instant messaging program, released as a standalone download in May 1997, that let you chat in real time with a list of friends under a screen name. Through the late 1990s and 2000s it was the main way many American teenagers and college students talked online, famous for its buddy lists, away messages and door sounds. As texting, Facebook and smartphone apps took over, use faded, and AOL shut AIM down on December 15, 2017.

body: You signed in with a screen name, often a mix of a nickname, a hobby and some numbers, and a small window showed your Buddy List: the friends you had added, sorted into groups you named yourself, showing who was online. A door creaking open meant a friend had just signed on; a door slamming shut meant they had left. Messages arrived with a chime in their own window.

When you stepped away you set an away message, a short status that anyone messaging you would see automatically. Away messages turned into a small art form of song lyrics, inside jokes and pointed hints aimed at one person. Your profile could hold more of the same.

A "chat war" with Microsoft: AOL blocks MSN Messenger from connecting to AIM
One report puts AIM at 52% of the instant messaging market, mainly in North America
A new logo replaces the yellow "Running Man" mascot; he returns in 2013
AOL announces the shutdown on October 6; AIM goes offline on December 15

body: Chat moved to phones and social networks. Texting, social networks and smartphone messaging apps did the same job without a separate desktop program, and AOL cut AIM's development staff in 2012. When it announced the end in 2017, AOL said the way people communicate had "profoundly changed". Buddy lists and other AIM data were deleted at the shutdown; AIM.com email addresses kept working.

No. AOL's servers have been off since December 2017, so the official AIM programs and apps no longer connect, and the buddy lists stored on them were deleted. What is left is memory: screenshots of old away messages and the sound files, which are widely shared online.

ul: The door-opening and door-slamming sounds as friends signed on and off
Writing the perfect away message, often a song lyric
Waiting to see whether your crush would sign on after school
Picking a screen name you would later be embarrassed by

faq.a: On December 15, 2017. AOL, then owned by Verizon, announced the decision on October 6, 2017.

faq.q: What was an AIM away message?
faq.a: A short status you set when you were not at your computer. Anyone who messaged you saw it as an automatic reply, so people filled them with lyrics, jokes and hints.

faq.q: Did you need AOL to use AIM?
faq.a: No. From 1997 AIM was a free standalone program, so anyone with an internet connection could create a screen name, AOL subscriber or not.
